exactBefore.body:
## Chef's Note

This banana bread is designed for freezer storage. The key to a perfect slice every morning is using Greek yogurt instead of butter to create a dense, moist texture that survives the freezing process without becoming crumbly. We blend the bananas and wet ingredients in a blender to create a smooth mixture before folding in the flour - this ensures even distribution of sweetness and prevents mushy pockets.

## Directions

1.  **The Emulsion:** Preheat oven to 350°F. In a blender, combine bananas, maple syrup, vanilla, cinnamon, egg, yogurt, and milk. Blend on high for 30 seconds until perfectly smooth.
2.  **Dry Mix:** In a large bowl, whisk together the whole-wheat flour, baking soda, and baking powder.
3.  **Combine:** Pour the wet ingredients into the dry. Stir with a spatula until **just combined** (do not over-mix, or the whole-wheat will turn tough).
4.  **Bake:** Pour into a greased loaf pan. Bake for 50-55 minutes until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.
5.  **Cool:** Let cool in the pan for 15 minutes before slicing.
6.  **The Freeze:** To store, slice the loaf into 1/2-inch rounds. Place parchment between slices and freeze in a zip-top bag. Reheat individual slices in the toaster for a Crunch finish.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 350°F. Grease a loaf pan with {{ingredients}}. Have a second small loaf pan available if the batter would come close to the rim; the batter needs clear space to rise.

steps.title: Blend the wet ingredients

steps.title: Fold and fill
steps.text: Pour the wet mixture into the dry ingredients. Fold with a spatula just until no dry flour remains. Scrape into the greased loaf pan and level gently. If there is insufficient space above the batter for it to rise, divide the batch between the prepared pans instead of filling to the rim.

steps.title: Bake through the center
steps.text: Bake at 350°F. For a full-batch loaf, begin checking at about 50 minutes; use 50–55 minutes as a starting range. Check smaller loaves earlier and remove them separately as they finish. The center should be set, and a thin knife inserted into the middle in a few places should come out without wet batter; moist crumbs are fine. A food thermometer provides another check: look for 200–205°F in the center, with no cooler raw section nearby. Avoid touching the pan with the probe. Continue baking until these cues agree; loosely tent the top with foil if it browns before the center is done.

steps.title: Cool completely
steps.text: Let the bread rest in its pan for about 15 minutes. Loosen the edges, turn out carefully onto a rack, and leave until completely cool before slicing or wrapping.

steps.title: Slice and freeze
steps.text: Cut crosswise into roughly ½-inch slices. For the original batch, expect roughly 12 slices; the actual count depends on the pan and the thickness you cut. Separate slices with parchment, wrap in airtight portions, then place in a freezer bag or airtight freezer container. Freeze promptly after cooling and packing.

steps.title: Serve a slice
steps.text: Unwrap a slice and thaw it at room temperature or toast it directly from frozen. Use gentle toaster or toaster-oven heat until warmed to your liking; take care with a slice that is too small or fragile for an upright toaster.

learning.focus: Bake the moist center fully and cool before packing slices.
learning.outcome: A set loaf that can be portioned and wrapped without trapping steam.
before: Grease the loaf pan and make sure the batter has clear space above it to rise; use an additional pan if needed.

checkpoints.cue: No dry flour remains, and the batter sits below the rim with room to rise.
checkpoints.why: Gentle mixing limits toughness, and headroom keeps the rising batter contained.

checkpoints.cue: The center is set, a thin knife shows no wet batter in several places, and a temperature check reads about 200–205°F through the center.
checkpoints.why: A browned top or one clean probe insertion can miss an underbaked pocket.

checkpoints.cue: After the brief pan rest, the loaf cools fully on a rack before cutting.
checkpoints.why: The crumb continues setting as it cools, and airtight wrapping should not trap warm steam.

troubleshooting.problem: The surface is browned but the center is still wet.
troubleshooting.cause: Pan depth, banana size or oven heat has changed the center-set time.
troubleshooting.fix: Tent loosely with foil and continue baking; check the center again rather than relying on the original clock.

troubleshooting.problem: Warm slices compress or shed wet crumbs.
troubleshooting.cause: The loaf was sliced before cooling, or the center was underbaked.
troubleshooting.fix: Let a fully baked loaf cool completely before slicing; for the next batch, check several center positions before removing it.

substitutions.alternative: Use honey in place of the syrup at the listed amount.
substitutions.effect: Honey changes the flavor; retain the rest of the formula and use the same center checks.

learning.storage: When fully cool, separate slices with parchment, wrap airtight in small portions and freeze at 0°F. For best quality, plan to use within about 3 months. Thaw unwrapped slices at room temperature or toast directly from frozen. Keep unused frozen portions sealed.
learning.timing: Allow about 20–25 minutes of hands-on preparation and packing, a starting bake of 50–55 minutes, and roughly 1–2 hours for full cooling after the 15-minute pan rest. Plan on about 2½–3½ hours through packing; a deep pan can need a longer bake or cool. Full cooling is the endpoint before wrapping. Smaller loaves and scaled batches need their own center checks; times do not multiply with ingredients.

exactAfter.body:
## Chef's Note

Ripe bananas, maple syrup and Greek yogurt make this a simple whole-wheat loaf with no added butter or oil in the batter. Blend the wet ingredients for an even mixture, fold in the flour gently, and let the bread cool all the way through before slicing it for the freezer.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Heat the oven to 350°F. Grease a loaf pan with nonstick spray. Have a second small loaf pan available if the batter would come close to the rim; the batter needs clear space to rise.
2. **Blend the wet ingredients:** Combine medium ripe bananas, maple syrup, large egg, plain Greek yogurt, milk of choice, ground cinnamon, and vanilla extract in a blender. Blend just until smooth, about 30 seconds, scraping the container as needed.
3. **Mix the dry ingredients:** In a large bowl, whisk whole-wheat flour, baking powder, and baking soda together until the leaveners are evenly distributed.
4. **Fold and fill:** Pour the wet mixture into the dry ingredients. Fold with a spatula just until no dry flour remains. Scrape into the greased loaf pan and level gently. If there is insufficient space above the batter for it to rise, divide the batch between the prepared pans instead of filling to the rim.
5. **Bake through the center:** Bake at 350°F. For a full-batch loaf, begin checking at about 50 minutes; use 50–55 minutes as a starting range. Check smaller loaves earlier and remove them separately as they finish. The center should be set, and a thin knife inserted into the middle in a few places should come out without wet batter; moist crumbs are fine. A food thermometer provides another check: look for 200–205°F in the center, with no cooler raw section nearby. Avoid touching the pan with the probe. Continue baking until these cues agree; loosely tent the top with foil if it browns before the center is done.
6. **Cool completely:** Let the bread rest in its pan for about 15 minutes. Loosen the edges, turn out carefully onto a rack, and leave until completely cool before slicing or wrapping.
7. **Slice and freeze:** Cut crosswise into roughly ½-inch slices. For the original batch, expect roughly 12 slices; the actual count depends on the pan and the thickness you cut. Separate slices with parchment, wrap in airtight portions, then place in a freezer bag or airtight freezer container. Freeze promptly after cooling and packing.
8. **Serve a slice:** Unwrap a slice and thaw it at room temperature or toast it directly from frozen. Use gentle toaster or toaster-oven heat until warmed to your liking; take care with a slice that is too small or fragile for an upright toaster.
